title: Stabilize SSE: recover interleaved heartbeats, prevent duplicate delimiters, and normalize escaped JSON boundaries
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers observed malformed JSON in streaming OpenAI-compatible endpoints when server-side heartbeats interleaved with data frames and when UTF-8 escape sequences were split across chunk boundaries. This caused partial-object emissions, duplicate delimiters, and out-of-order function-call sentinels under load. This PR introduces a resilient reassembly state machine, a heartbeat coalescer that marks and defers delimiter emission while preserving token order, and an escape-boundary normalizer that rewrites split UTF-8/JSON escapes before attempting JSON incremental parse. Work done: - Implement sse/reassembly.go: compact state machine with seq-window, acked-offsets, and a soft-resume path for truncated frames. - Add heartbeat_coalescer in runtime/streaming: buffers interleaved "ping" events and merges adjacent delimiter tokens into a single canonical delimiter upon flush. - Introduce escape_normalizer in compat/openai_stream.go: maintains a two-byte lookbehind to fix split "\u" and multibyte UTF-8 escapes at chunk edges. - Tests: new unit and integration coverage under tests/sse_reassembly_test.go and tests/stream_chaos_integration.yaml (simulated TCP stalls, heartbeat bursts, partial writes). - Docs: note in docs/streaming.md about reassembly guarantees and developer-visible delimiters. Checklist: - [x] Core reassembly state machine implemented - [x] Heartbeat coalescing and canonical delimiter rewriting - [x] Escape normalization with minimal copying - [x] Regression tests for partial JSON, duplicate delimiters, function-call sentinel ordering - [x] E2E chaos test reproducing customer symptom - [x] Benchmarked impact: ~+2% CPU at peak under synthetic load. Commits summary: 5 commits (split tasks): 1) reassembly model + tests, 2) heartbeat coalescer, 3) escape normalizer + compat hooks, 4) integration tests and benchmarks, 5) docs and changelog. Files changed (high-level): - sse/reassembly.go: new - runtime/streaming/heartbeat_coalescer.go: new - compat/openai_stream.go: changes to streaming handler and resync points - tests/sse_reassembly_test.go: new - tests/stream_chaos_integration.yaml: new - docs/streaming.md: updated - pkg/tracing/stream_span.go: minor instrumentation - Makefile/CICD: add chaos job The fix is intentionally conservative: when the reassembly state detects an irrecoverable mid-object loss we emit an explicit <REPAIR> marker event (consumers can interpret this) and request client-level retry semantics; we avoid silent object truncation. Review timeline: - Initial draft posted 2026-02-14 - First pass review requested changes around lock contention and memory copies (LM); author reduced allocations by using a ring buffer. - Second pass asked for clearer sentinel ordering guarantees; added unit test for function-call sentinel ordering under interleaved heartbeats (ZM). - CI initially failed lint on import ordering; fixed. CI: 12 checks (unit, integration, lint, go vet, typescript build), final status: all passing. Merge: Squash-merged on 2026-02-28 after approvals and green CI. Notes for consumers: This patch tightens stream semantics: - Delimiters are now canonical on emission; mid-stream duplicate delimiters will be squashed. - Small chance of +2% CPU under pathological heartbeat rates; recommend enabling coalescer only for endpoints with heartbeat use via config flag streaming.heartbeat_coalesce=true. Backcompat: non-breaking for protocol consumers; but consumers relying on duplicate delimiter semantics should be updated. Related: ENG-4218 (customer incident), ENG-4301 (runtime reassembly agenda).

release_notes: Fix streaming JSON truncation and delimiter duplication: resilient SSE reassembly, heartbeat coalescing, and escape normalization. Improves OpenAI-compatible streaming stability under interleaved heartbeats; enable via streaming.heartbeat_coalesce=true if desired.
